thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What are the 5 rules for creating an immutable class in Java?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: 1. Declare class as final (prevent subclass overriding). 2. Make all fields private and final. 3. Do not provide any mutator methods. 4. Ensure exclusive access to any mutable components via defensive copying in constructors and accessors. 5. Initialize all fields fully in constructors.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why is Collections.unmodifiableList(list) not enough by itself in a constructor?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: unmodifiableList wraps the list you give it, but it does NOT copy it! If the caller still holds a reference to the original ArrayList, they can call originalList.add(item) and the 'unmodifiable' wrapper will reflect the change! You must make a new copy first, THEN wrap it.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why is immutability crucial in multithreaded systems?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: Immutable objects cannot change state after construction. Multiple threads can read an immutable object simultaneously without synchronization locks, thread contention, or race conditions. They are inherently thread-safe.

# Immutable Order & Cart System (Java OOP)

## Overview
A thread-safe financial order processing engine built in Java demonstrating strict immutability, Value Objects, and defensive copying to eliminate reference leakage and aliasing vulnerabilities.

## The 5 Rules of Immutability Applied
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                 5 Rules of Immutability                     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Final Class:       Prevents subclass extension/override  |
| 2. Final Fields:      Prevents post-construction mutation   |
| 3. No Mutators:       Zero setter methods anywhere          |
| 4. Defensive Copies:  Constructor copies mutable collections|
| 5. Safe Accessors:    Returns Collections.unmodifiableList  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Architecture Blueprint
```
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
|       <<final>>       |              |       <<final>>       |
|         Order         |<>----------->|       OrderItem       |
+-----------------------+ (Defensive   +-----------------------+
| - orderId: String     |  Copy)       | - sku: String         |
| - customerId: String  |              | - name: String        |
| - items: List<Item>   |              | - quantity: int       |
| - timestamp: long     |              | - unitPrice: Money    |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
| + computeTotal(): Mny |                         |
| + getItems(): List    |                         v Has-A
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
                                       |       <<final>>       |
                                       |         Money         |
                                       +-----------------------+
                                       | - amount: double      |
                                       | - currency: String    |
                                       +-----------------------+
                                       | + add(Money): Money   |
                                       +-----------------------+
```

## How to Run
```bash
javac Money.java OrderItem.java Order.java OrderApp.java
java OrderApp
```

## Sample Invoice Output
```text
=======================================================
                  SETTLED INVOICE                      
=======================================================
Order ID:    ORD-2026-9042
Customer ID: CUST-8812
Timestamp:   2026-10-03T10:15:00Z
Status:      FINALIZED / IMMUTABLE
-------------------------------------------------------
ITEMS:
 1. [SKU-KB]  Mechanical Keyboard   x1 @ $120.00 = $120.00
 2. [SKU-MS]  Optical Mouse         x2 @  $40.00 =  $80.00
-------------------------------------------------------
Total Amount Due: $200.00 USD
=======================================================
Anti-Aliasing Test: External list modified -> Placed Order is 100% UNCHANGED.
```

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What are the 5 rules for creating an immutable class in Java?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: 1. Declare class as final (prevent subclass overriding). 2. Make all fields private and final. 3. Do not provide any mutator methods. 4. Ensure exclusive access to any mutable components via defensive copying in constructors and accessors. 5. Initialize all fields fully in constructors.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why is Collections.unmodifiableList(list) not enough by itself in a constructor?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: unmodifiableList wraps the list you give it, but it does NOT copy it! If the caller still holds a reference to the original ArrayList, they can call originalList.add(item) and the 'unmodifiable' wrapper will reflect the change! You must make a new copy first, THEN wrap it.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why is immutability crucial in multithreaded systems?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: Immutable objects cannot change state after construction. Multiple threads can read an immutable object simultaneously without synchronization locks, thread contention, or race conditions. They are inherently thread-safe.

# Immutable Order & Cart System (Java OOP)

## Overview
A thread-safe financial order processing engine built in Java demonstrating strict immutability, Value Objects, and defensive copying to eliminate reference leakage and aliasing vulnerabilities.

## The 5 Rules of Immutability Applied
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                 5 Rules of Immutability                     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Final Class:       Prevents subclass extension/override  |
| 2. Final Fields:      Prevents post-construction mutation   |
| 3. No Mutators:       Zero setter methods anywhere          |
| 4. Defensive Copies:  Constructor copies mutable collections|
| 5. Safe Accessors:    Returns Collections.unmodifiableList  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Architecture Blueprint
```
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
|       <<final>>       |              |       <<final>>       |
|         Order         |<>----------->|       OrderItem       |
+-----------------------+ (Defensive   +-----------------------+
| - orderId: String     |  Copy)       | - sku: String         |
| - customerId: String  |              | - name: String        |
| - items: List<Item>   |              | - quantity: int       |
| - timestamp: long     |              | - unitPrice: Money    |
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
| + computeTotal(): Mny |                         |
| + getItems(): List    |                         v Has-A
+-----------------------+              +-----------------------+
                                       |       <<final>>       |
                                       |         Money         |
                                       +-----------------------+
                                       | - amount: double      |
                                       | - currency: String    |
                                       +-----------------------+
                                       | + add(Money): Money   |
                                       +-----------------------+
```

## How to Run
```bash
javac Money.java OrderItem.java Order.java OrderApp.java
java OrderApp
```
